Subject: MAP & procurement sequencing for VantageMed pilot

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. VantageMed’s pilot scope looks like a great fit for our low-latency inference tier. To keep momentum with procurement and legal, Id like to propose a short mutual action plan (MAP) that sequences MSA / DPA / Order Form activities alongside the evaluation milestones. Goal is to get a signed order form and environment access within the quarter while protecting both sides on data handling.

Quick asks from our side: can you confirm the procurement cadence and the VantageMed legal teams preferred review window? Also, does procurement require an executed DPA before test data is ingested?

Ive attached a first-pass MAP (VantageMed_MAP_v1.xlsx) — it suggests milestone due dates, owners, and dependencies (MSA signature → Order Form → Prod onboarding). If that works, well loop in our Legal (Monica) to start a light redline on the MSA so your counsel has something concrete to react to.

Proposed top-level milestones (high-level):
- Week 1 (this week): Align on MAP and evaluation test plan
- Week 2–3: MSA redline exchange and security questionnaire
- Week 3–4: Order Form draft and commercial approvals
- Week 5: Target signature and pilot environment provisioning

If you prefer a different order (e.g., Order Form first + MSA post-signature for PO-led customers), we can flip the flow — want to make sure were matching VantageMeds procurement rules.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync to lock dates.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: VantageMed_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@vantagemed.com>

Subject: Re: MAP & procurement sequencing for VantageMed pilot

Diego —

Appreciate the MAP. Procurement's cadence here is fairly tight because were consolidating multiple vendor pilots this quarter. High level:
- Procurement needs a completed order form and PO approval to start provisioning (we can issue a PO against signed order form).
- Legal (copied) wants to complete MSA redline before contract signature, but can accept limited signature exceptions documented in writing.
- The DPA is non-negotiable for test data if PHI is involved; otherwise a standard DPA template can run in parallel.

Concrete timeline from our side:
- 26 Mar–31 Mar: Internal procurement review; Tom will gather commercial targets.
- 1 Apr–7 Apr: Legal redline window (Elena will lead).
- 8 Apr: Target for signed order form / PO issuance.

Were pushing to have a PO in hand by 8 Apr so we can start the pilot in the second week of April. Regarding order: we prefer to have the MSA redlines exchanged early but can sign the order form conditioned on an agreed MSA redline timeline if Redwood is comfortable.

On the DPA: we will need an executed DPA prior to any test datasets containing PHI; for synthetic or de-identified test data we can accept a signed DPA or a documented interim agreement.

Tom will share procurement contact notes separately.

—Sara
Sara Lin
Head of Platform Integrations | VantageMed

Subject: Re: MAP & procurement sequencing for VantageMed pilot — evaluation details

Thanks Sara — quick note on the evaluation dependencies so the MAP reflects what we actually need to complete the pilot:

1) Environment provisioning: we need a short order form to allocate dedicated test capacity (slot reservation) — this can be a minimal commercial commitment to cover the pilot window.
2) Data access & DPA: for PHI scenarios we require DPA executed before provisioning. For synthetic data we can proceed with an interim DPA or an executed annex that limits data types.
3) Security evidence: SOC 2 report + encryption at-rest/in-transit + KMS integration details. Monica can coordinate a narrow security questionnaire; ideally the security exchange occurs during the MSA redline window.
4) Timeboxed acceptance criteria: sample prompts, latency SLOs, and cost limits — we should put these in the MAP so procurement knows how to size the pilot.

Ill prepare a two-page evaluation scope (attached: Evaluation_Scope_vantage-test-plan.pdf) with acceptance criteria and required artifacts. Diego — if procurement insists on the order form first, we should still push to get the MSA redline started concurrently.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Evaluation_Scope_vantage-test-plan.pdf
